data.paper_title: Profitability of Momentum Strategies: An Evaluation of Alternative Explanations
data.selected_experiment: Table 1, decile momentum portfolios (P1-P10) formed on past six-month returns and held six months, NYSE/AMEX stocks priced above $5, 1965-1989 / 1990-1997 / 1965-1997

economic_rationale.value: Momentum profits are attributed to investors underreacting or delayed-overreacting to information (behavioral models), rather than to cross-sectional dispersion in expected returns as Conrad and Kaul argue.

evidence.quote: The behavioral models specify that the holding period returns arise because of a delayed overreaction to information that push the prices of winners (losers) above (below) their long-term values.

universe_and_filters.value: All NYSE/AMEX stocks, excluding NASDAQ stocks and excluding stocks priced below $5 at the beginning of the holding period.

evidence.quote: We follow JT and include all NYSE/AMEX stocks and exclude NASDAQ stocks.

At the end of each month we rank the stocks in the sample based on their past six-month returns (month —5 to month 0) and then group the stocks into ten equally weighted portfolios based on these ranks.

signal_formula_words.value: Past six-month cumulative return over months -5 to 0 relative to the ranking date; stocks are ranked on this return.

evidence.quote: To increase the power of our tests we construct overlapping portfolios.

breakpoints.value: Ten groups by rank of past six-month returns (P1 is the ten percent of stocks with highest returns, P10 the ten percent with lowest); whether NYSE-only breakpoints are used is not stated.

evidence.quote: P1 is the equal-weighted portfolio of ten percent of the stocks with the highest six-month lagged returns, P2 is the equal-weighted portfolio of the ten percent of the stocks with the next highest returns and so on.

favored_group.value: P1 (past winners: highest past six-month return decile)

evidence.quote: Portfolio P1 is comprised of stocks with the best ranking period returns and PlO is comprised of stocks with the worst ranking period returns.

disfavored_group.value: P10 (past losers: lowest past six-month return decile)

evidence.quote: Portfolio P1 is comprised of stocks with the best ranking period returns and PlO is comprised of stocks with the worst ranking period returns.

weighting_evidence.quote: P1 is the equal-weighted portfolio of ten percent of the stocks with the highest six-month lagged returns, P2 is the equal-weighted portfolio of the ten percent of the stocks with the next highest returns and so on.

expected_sign_evidence.quote: The table reveals a monotonic relation between returns and momentum ranks over the 1965 to 1989 sample period, confirming the results in JT.

headline_result.value: P1-P10 difference of 1.11% per month (t=4.61) in 1965-1989, 1.01% per month in 1990-1997, and 1.09% per month (t=5.65) in 1965-1997

evidence.quote: The difference between the P1 and PlO portfolio returns is 1.11% per month, which is reliably different from zero.
